strengths: Well-motivated and elegant approach that combines neural operators with diffusion in a principled way, preserving discretization invariance while enabling efficient probabilistic modeling
Strong theoretical contributions: Proposition 2.3 connects velocity matching to Wasserstein distance with rigorous proofs; Proposition 4.1 establishes recovery of optimal rank-r KL expansions

Comprehensive experimental evaluation covering stochastic PDEs, deterministic long-horizon rollouts, multiple baselines, and extensive ablations; results demonstrate clear improvements in capturing spatial structure of uncertainty

Practical advantages including modularity (works with any backbone), parameter efficiency compared to autoencoders, efficient sampling in coefficient space, and demonstrated compatibility with different architectures

Rigorous presentation with clear problem formulation, complete proofs, detailed experimental protocols, and transparent discussion of limitations; high reproducibility with implementation details and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: combines existing techniques (operator encoders, latent diffusion) in a useful but incremental way; primarily an engineering contribution rather than fundamental innovation

Inconsistent empirical improvements: pixel-space diffusion outperforms DLL on Kolmogorov flow (NRMSE 0.369 vs 0.426, CRPS 0.692 vs 0.822); performance heavily dependent on backbone quality; method trades mean accuracy for uncertainty quantification

Operator encoder design underjustified: Assumption A.11 (universal approximation) is strong but never empirically validated; reconstruction can be worse than autoencoders on stochastic problems (Tables 6-7); no principled method for choosing rank r (ablations show non-monotonic behavior)

Uncertainty quantification claims lack rigor: Section 3.3 claims diffusion underfitting indicates epistemic uncertainty in deterministic settings but this is heuristic without calibration guarantees; authors acknowledge this is not a true epistemic uncertainty guarantee but use it anyway

Scalability and scope limitations: experiments restricted to small grids (256×256 max), regular domains only, synthetic benchmarks only; no real-world evaluation; two-stage training adds complexity; no computational cost comparisons provided

Parameter count fairness issues: DM/LDM are 5-8× larger than FNO methods (Table 8); unclear if their better performance reflects architectural advantages or capacity advantage; DLL encoder can exceed autoencoder size in 2D (Table 9)

Reconstruction quality degradation on stochastic problems not adequately addressed: Tables 6-7 show operator encoder reconstruction substantially worse than autoencoders, directly impacting downstream diffusion quality but minimally discussed

Missing empirical analysis: no failure mode discussion, no discretization invariance validation, minimal exploration of sensitivity to encoder training quality, no investigation of why r=64 is optimal despite non-monotonic ablations
